newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV posts higher 96 profit, ups dividend.
newsitem.headline: OMV posts higher 96 profit, ups dividend.

text.p: Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV reported a 14 percent rise in 1996 net profit on Tuesday, thanks to cost-cutting and consistently high crude oil prices, and said it was raising its dividend by three schillings (24 cents) to 23.

"1996 was a very successful year for OMV. It is especially gratifying that all six business sectors posted positive earnings before interest and tax (EBIT)," OMV said in a statement released ahead of a news conference.

Net profit climbed to 1.98 billion schillings from 1.73 billion the previous year. Pre-tax earnings jumped 42 percent to 2.97 billion schillings, beating 1995's record 2.09 billion. EBIT was 33 percent higher at 2.92 billion schillings.
Austria's biggest industrial group said it was confident of posting another good set of earnings in 1997, despite a recent reversal in crude oil prices.

"From today's point of view we can expect with confidence a good earnings development in 1997. Some sectors will see a deterioration in the business environment while others will see an improvement," OMV said, without giving further details.
Gas continued to supply the lion's share of OMV's operating revenue last year. Gas EBIT increased to 1.77 billion schillings from 1.73 billion.

OMV said extending its gas pipeline network would take up much of the more than six billion schillings in annual investment planned for the next three years. Austria, at the heart of Europe, is an important transit point for Russian gas supplies to the west.
Exploration and production (E&P) and marketing returned to the black in 1996 and OMV said both sectors would benefit from investment spending in 1997.

E&P, boosted by last year's high crude oil prices and a stronger dollar, posted an EBIT of 0.39 billion schillings after a loss of 0.25 billion. OMV said secured oil reserves rose to 26.21 million tonnes from 25.27 million, thanks to new discoveries in Austria and the North Sea.
Marketing EBIT rose to 0.12 billion schillings after a loss of 0.06 billion in 1995.
Only refining, plagued by poor margins, saw a decline in operating profit. EBIT fell to 0.12 billion schillings from 0.62 billion in 1995.

OMV shares in Vienna were up three schillings at 1,341 in a generally firm market. Traders noted that the figures confirmed provisional results released by OMV in February. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254 ($ = 12.07 Austrian Schillings)
